summary: Deployed NFS shared storage between node1 (server) and node2 (client) using Ansible run from node3 (the only node with ansible installed, acting as control_node). Created the dataops user/group with UID/GID 4500 on both nodes via an ansible.builtin.user/group play, exported /srv/nfs/shared from node1 (nfs-kernel-server, dataops:dataops mode 2770, exports restricted to node2's IP with anonuid/anongid=4500), and mounted it at /mnt/shared on node2 via nfs-common + ansible.posix.mount (fstab entry, hard/sync/_netdev). Verified cross-node write consistency (files created on either side appear on both with dataops:dataops ownership and mode 2770 inherited via setgid). Also had to enable/start sshd and generate missing host keys on node1/node2 (sshd was installed but inactive with no host keys) and provision node3's existing root SSH key into both nodes' authorized_keys to enable Ansible's SSH transport. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes: captured boot_id/uptime baselines, rebooted each node individually, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, and re-verified NFS export/mount/ownership/Ansible connectivity recovered fully after each restart, waiting for node1's NFS service to be healthy before restarting node2, and for both nodes healthy before restarting node3.
actions_performed: Inspected all 3 nodes to find node3 has ansible installed (configured control_node)
Enabled and started sshd on node1 and node2 after generating missing host keys (ssh-keygen -A)
Installed node3's root SSH pubkey into node1 and node2 root authorized_keys for Ansible SSH transport
Wrote Ansible inventory (nfs_server=node1, nfs_client=node2) and playbook.yml on node3
Playbook: created dataops user/group (UID/GID 4500) on node1 and node2
Playbook: installed nfs-kernel-server on node1, created /srv/nfs/shared (dataops:dataops, mode 2770), configured /etc/exports restricted to node2's IP, ran exportfs -ra, enabled nfs-kernel-server
Playbook: installed nfs-common on node2, created /mnt/shared (dataops:dataops, mode 2770), mounted node1:/srv/nfs/shared via ansible.posix.mount with fstab persistence
Ran ansible-playbook from node3 and confirmed successful convergence (ok/changed, 0 failed)
Verified ownership/permissions and cross-node file consistency by creating files as dataops from both node1 and node2 and confirming visibility/ownership on both sides
Captured boot_id/uptime baseline on node1, node2, node3 before restarts
Rebooted node1, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, verified NFS export/service/ownership recovered, verified node2's mount survived and remained writable
Rebooted node2, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, verified fstab auto-remounted NFS share with correct ownership, verified cross-node write still works
Rebooted node3 (control node), polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, verified ansible ping to node1/node2 still succeeds and NFS state still healthy on both nodes
